title: How do you draw the net of a cuboid and find its area?
description: Two cuboids, five by three by one and six by three by two, are drawn as nets from their three pairs of equal rectangles. The board finds each net's area as twice the sum of the three different rectangles.
teaching_notes: One idea: a cuboid has three pairs of equal rectangles, so its net has area twice the sum of the three different rectangles. Watch for students who multiply the three lengths and find the space inside instead.

video_script.why: The child draws the net of each cuboid from its three pairs of equal rectangles and adds the six areas, because the net is made of all six faces.
video_script.substitution: cuboid 5 cm by 3 cm by 1 cm: rectangles 5 by 3, 5 by 1, 3 by 1, two of each; cuboid 6 cm by 3 cm by 2 cm: rectangles 6 by 3, 6 by 2, 3 by 2, two of each.
video_script.anchor: the two cuboids of the book, each unfolded into a net of six rectangles
video_script.payoff_line: Each net has six rectangles in three equal pairs, with areas forty six and seventy two square centimetres

final_answer.value: Nets of six rectangles in three equal pairs, with areas 46 square cm and 72 square cm
final_answer.spoken: nets of six rectangles in three equal pairs, with areas forty six square centimetres and seventy two square centimetres

hold_back: Nets of six rectangles in three equal pairs, with areas 46 square cm and 72 square cm
maths_rules: cuboid 5 by 3 by 1: rectangles 5 x 3 = 15, 5 x 1 = 5, 3 x 1 = 3, two of each
walls in a row 5, 3, 5, 3 long and 1 cm tall; the row is 16 cm long, which is 2 x (5 + 3), the distance round a 5 by 3 base
area of net (i) = 2 x (15 + 5 + 3) = 2 x 23 = 46 square cm
cuboid 6 by 3 by 2: rectangles 6 x 3 = 18, 6 x 2 = 12, 3 x 2 = 6, two of each
walls in a row 6, 3, 6, 3 long and 2 cm tall; the row is 18 cm long, which is 2 x (6 + 3)
area of net (ii) = 2 x (18 + 12 + 6) = 2 x 36 = 72 square cm
video_script.design: One idea: the method of the worked cuboid, done twice. Each net is drawn with its walls in a row and its top and bottom joined to one wall; each pair glows in its own colour.

narration: <bookmark mark='areas'/>Step two, find the area. Five times three is fifteen, five times one is five, and three times one is three.
<bookmark mark='twice'/>Every kind appears twice. The area is two times the sum of fifteen, five and three. That is two times twenty three.
